name: Boston
title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Boston, MA | Genstone
metaDescription: Boston investor rehabs for triple-deckers, rowhouses and two-families: free pre-offer review, ISD permits, deleading scope and draws tied to finished work.
intro:
Boston rehab math is unforgiving. Acquisition prices are high, the housing is old, and a single surprise behind a plaster wall in a Dorchester triple-decker can erase the spread you underwrote. Genstone Construction works with investors, lenders, servicers and funds who buy in Boston and want the repair number pinned down before the offer goes in, not after the walls are open.

We start with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review that estimates repairs, pressure-tests your after-repair value and tells you whether the deal still works at your price. If it does, you get a written scope with labor, materials and a draw schedule, often in more than one finish level so you can compare a rental-grade plan against a resale plan. Genstone coordinates vetted, licensed local contractors in Greater Boston under one field manager, handles permits through the city's Inspectional Services Department, and ties every draw to work that is actually complete. There is no upfront payment, and the final payment comes after you approve the finished job.
housingStock:
Most of what investors buy in Boston was built before 1940, and a large share of it before 1910. The signature building is the wood-frame triple-decker, three stacked flats with front porches, found by the thousands in Dorchester, Roxbury, Jamaica Plain, East Boston and South Boston. Alongside them sit two-family 'double-deckers', mansard-roofed Victorians in Roslindale and Hyde Park, and brick or brownstone rowhouses in the South End, Charlestown and Back Bay. West Roxbury and parts of Hyde Park add mid-century Capes, Colonials and ranches that behave more like suburban houses.

That age shapes every scope. Triple-deckers are often balloon-framed, which means open stud cavities can run from the basement to the attic and carry fire, air and mice between floors. Foundations are commonly fieldstone or brick with mortar that has washed out over a century of wet springs, and many basements see water every thaw. Original wiring may be knob-and-tube or early cloth-insulated cable, sometimes extended with whatever the last owner found at the hardware store. Heating is frequently a converted coal boiler now running on oil or gas, feeding cast-iron radiators through steam or gravity hot-water piping wrapped in asbestos insulation.

Lead paint is close to universal. Massachusetts has its own Lead Law on top of federal rules, and an owner who rents to a family with a child under six must have the unit deleaded, so the paint question is a scope and budget item from day one rather than a footnote.

The rowhouses bring different problems: party walls shared with neighbors, deep narrow floor plans that make kitchens and bathrooms hard to relocate, slate or flat membrane roofs, and exterior work that may need sign-off in a landmark or architectural conservation district. A realistic Boston scope accounts for these conditions up front instead of discovering them in demolition.

commonIssues.title: Lead paint and deleading
commonIssues.body: Nearly every pre-1978 Boston property carries lead paint on trim, windows, porches and stair parts. The Massachusetts Lead Law requires deleading when a child under six lives in a rental unit, and federal RRP rules govern how disturbed paint is handled during any renovation. On a triple-decker that can mean window replacement, porch work and friction-surface treatments in three separate units. We scope it explicitly so it never shows up as a change order.

commonIssues.title: Balloon framing and fire blocking
commonIssues.body: Older triple-deckers and Victorians often have continuous stud bays from sill to rafters. Once walls are opened for wiring or plumbing, inspectors expect fire blocking at each floor line, and insulating those bays without proper blocking creates its own problems. Planning this before demolition keeps rough inspections from stalling and lets electricians and insulators work in the right order. Skipping it is a common reason a Boston rough inspection fails.

commonIssues.title: Fieldstone foundations and wet basements
commonIssues.body: Rubble and fieldstone foundations under many Dorchester, Roxbury and Jamaica Plain houses lose mortar over time and let water in during snowmelt and heavy rain. Repointing, exterior grading, gutters routed away from the house and, where needed, interior drainage with a sump are common line items. A finished basement in one of these buildings is rarely worth the risk unless water is fully controlled first.

commonIssues.title: Old heating plants and oil tanks
commonIssues.body: Many Boston multifamilies still run original cast-iron boilers that were converted from coal, with asbestos wrap on the near-boiler piping and an oil tank in the basement. Tank removal involves the local fire department, and any sign of a leak can pull in state environmental reporting. Replacing boilers with high-efficiency gas units or adding heat pumps is a frequent part of a value-add plan.

commonIssues.title: Porches, decks and egress
commonIssues.body: Stacked front and rear porches are part of what makes a triple-decker work, and they take a beating from freeze-thaw cycles and road salt. Rotten posts, failing ledgers and undersized footings are common, and rear porches often double as a second means of egress. Rebuilding them to current code, with proper guardrails and connections, is usually a permit job and a priority for both safety and appraisal.

investorMarket:
Boston rewards investors who match the strategy to the neighborhood instead of forcing one plan everywhere. Dorchester, Mattapan, Roxbury and parts of Hyde Park hold most of the city's triple-deckers and two-families, and these buildings are the backbone of buy-and-hold and BRRRR plans: three rent rolls on one lot, steady demand near Red Line, Orange Line and commuter rail stops, and a refinance case built on income as much as comparable sales.

Jamaica Plain, Roslindale and West Roxbury lean owner-occupant. Single-families and condo-ready two-families there sell to buyers who notice finish quality, so flips and condo conversions make more sense than rental-grade turns. Spending on kitchens, baths and layout pays back in these areas in a way it often does not a mile away.

East Boston and South Boston have seen heavy redevelopment, which pushes acquisition prices up and squeezes the margin for light cosmetic flips. The deals that still work there tend to involve real structural or systems problems that scare off retail buyers. Brighton and Allston carry a large student and young-professional rental base, where durable finishes and fast unit turns matter more than design.

Across all of these, Boston's high entry prices mean the repair estimate carries more weight in the underwriting than it would in a lower-cost market. Getting a contractor's number before you commit capital is the single most useful thing you can do.
permits:
Building, electrical, plumbing and gas permits in Boston run through the Inspectional Services Department, known locally as ISD. Most rehab work beyond paint and flooring needs a permit: structural repairs, new or relocated plumbing fixtures, electrical service upgrades and rewiring, boiler and water heater replacement, window replacement that changes openings, porch and deck rebuilds, and any change in the number of units. Massachusetts requires licensed electricians, plumbers and gas fitters for that trade work, and building permits are pulled by a holder of a Construction Supervisor License, with Home Improvement Contractor registration required for work on owner-occupied one- to four-family homes.

ISD performs rough and final inspections for each trade. Plans that add units or change use can trigger zoning review, and some go to the Zoning Board of Appeal. Exterior work in the Back Bay, Beacon Hill, the South End and other landmark or architectural conservation districts needs approval from the relevant commission before permits issue. Sale of a residential property in Massachusetts also requires a smoke and carbon monoxide compliance certificate from the Boston Fire Department, which is worth scheduling well ahead of a listing or closing.
climate:
Boston winters are long, wet and windy rather than extremely cold, and that combination is hard on old buildings. Nor'easters drive rain and snow sideways into clapboard and window frames, and repeated freeze-thaw cycles open masonry joints and heave porch footings. Ice dams form on poorly insulated roofs, so attic air sealing and insulation are worth including in any scope that touches the roof.

Exterior work, roofing, masonry and foundation waterproofing schedule best between late spring and fall. Concrete and mortar need protection in cold weather, and exterior painting stalls once temperatures drop. Interior work continues year round, but vacant buildings need heat or a professional winterization during the cold months to protect plumbing. Low-lying parts of East Boston, Charlestown and South Boston near the harbor also face coastal flooding during storm surges, which affects where mechanicals and electrical panels should sit.

faqs.q: Does Genstone have an office in Boston?
faqs.a: Genstone Construction is headquartered in Romeoville, Illinois. In Boston we coordinate a vetted network of licensed and insured local contractors, with a designated field manager overseeing your project from scope to completion. Estimating, scheduling, draw management and documentation are handled by our team, and you can follow progress, photos and milestones without being on site. That structure is how we serve investors, lenders and servicers across many markets while the work itself is done by tradespeople who know Boston buildings and ISD inspectors.

faqs.q: How do you handle lead paint on a Boston rehab?
faqs.a: We assume lead is present in any pre-1978 building and scope for it from the start. That means RRP-compliant work practices whenever painted surfaces are disturbed, and where you plan to rent to families, a deleading plan that satisfies the Massachusetts Lead Law, often built around window replacement, trim and porch work. Putting it in the original estimate keeps it out of change orders and lets you compare the cost against your rent and resale assumptions.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a triple-decker with tenants in place?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Many investors buy partly occupied triple-deckers and renovate the vacant unit first, then rotate tenants as leases turn. Shared systems such as the roof, foundation, porches and service entrance need careful sequencing so occupied units keep heat, water and power. Your field manager plans the phasing, coordinates access with tenants and schedules inspections so each unit can be finished and rented without holding up the rest of the building.

faqs.q: How are payments structured?
faqs.a: There is no upfront payment. Your estimate includes a draw schedule tied to defined milestones, and each draw is released only after that work is completed and documented with photos and inspection results where applicable. Dumpsters and debris removal are included in the estimate rather than billed separately. Final payment comes after the job is complete and you have approved it. Lien waivers are collected as work is paid, which is important to lenders and servicers financing Boston projects.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Boston, MA | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Boston fix and flip renovations: pre-offer repair estimates, buyer-focused finishes for JP, Roslindale and Dorchester, ISD permits and draws tied to progress.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Boston
fix-flip.intro:
Flipping in Boston works when the purchase price leaves room for the old-house problems you cannot see from the open house. Buyers here are paying a premium and they arrive with inspectors who know exactly what a century-old Victorian hides. The flips that hold their margin are the ones where the scope was honest from the start: wiring, heat, water management and lead handled properly, then finishes chosen for the specific neighborhood's buyer.

Genstone Construction gives you a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review on the property before you commit, estimating repairs and checking your after-repair value against what similar renovated homes in that part of Boston actually sell for. Once you buy, a single field manager runs the job, coordinates licensed local trades, keeps ISD inspections moving and documents every draw so your lender and your partners can see where the money went.

sections.h2: Matching finishes to the Boston buyer
sections.body:
A flip in Jamaica Plain or Roslindale sells to a different buyer than one in Mattapan or Hyde Park, and the finish plan should reflect that. In JP and Roslindale, buyers compare your kitchen against renovated condos down the street, so layout, natural light and a convincing primary bath matter. Opening a cramped Victorian kitchen to the dining room is common, but in a balloon-framed house that often means a beam and an engineer, which belongs in the estimate on day one.

In Hyde Park, Mattapan and the southern parts of Dorchester, buyers are frequently first-time owners stretching to get in. They want clean, durable finishes, updated systems and a house that passes their inspection without a long repair list. Overspending on designer tile there rarely comes back at sale.

We often price more than one finish level so you can see the cost difference and decide based on the comps, not on a guess. Your estimate lists labor, materials and the draw schedule for each option, so the choice is a numbers decision you make before demolition starts.

sections.h2: What Boston inspectors and buyers will find
sections.body:
Buyers' home inspectors in Boston know the patterns of old housing, and they will flag the same items an experienced estimator looks for: ungrounded or knob-and-tube circuits, an aging boiler with asbestos-wrapped pipes, galvanized supply lines, a basement that shows efflorescence or water staining, and windows or porches that point to lead hazards. A flip that leaves those items in place invites a renegotiation after the inspection.

The better approach is to address them in the renovation and document the work. Permitted electrical and plumbing upgrades with ISD sign-offs, a new heating system, basement water control and properly handled lead surfaces turn into selling points in the listing rather than weaknesses. Genstone collects inspection results, photos and lien waivers as the project moves, which gives your listing agent a clean packet to share with buyers and their inspectors.

Plan the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the Boston Fire Department into the closing schedule as well, because a sale cannot close without it.

sections.h2: Controlling carrying cost on a Boston flip
sections.body:
Boston acquisition prices make every month of holding expensive, so schedule discipline matters as much as the budget. The biggest delays on local flips usually come from three places: permits that were filed late or incompletely, trades waiting on each other for rough inspections, and exterior work pushed into winter.

We file permits as soon as the scope is final and sequence the job so rough electrical, plumbing and framing inspections happen together where possible. When a flip closes in late fall, we front-load roofing, siding, porch and masonry work so the house is weathertight before nor'easter season, then finish interiors through the winter with heat on.

Draws are tied to completed milestones, so you are never paying ahead of the work, and you can see progress through photos and updates without driving to the site. That visibility helps when you are managing several projects or raising capital from partners who want regular reporting.

faqs.q: Which Boston neighborhoods work best for flips?
faqs.a: Flips tend to perform best where owner-occupants are the main buyers and renovated homes trade at a clear premium over unrenovated ones, which describes much of Jamaica Plain, Roslindale, West Roxbury and parts of Dorchester. Areas with heavy new construction can make cosmetic flips harder to justify because buyers have newer alternatives. A Pre-Offer Rehab Review on the specific property is the most reliable way to see whether the spread is there.

faqs.q: Do you handle condo conversions of two-families?
faqs.a: We renovate two-families intended for condo sale, including separating utilities, upgrading fire separation between units and meeting the code items that come with a change in ownership structure. Zoning approvals and condominium documents are handled by your attorney and design professionals, and we coordinate with them so the construction scope lines up with what the city approves and what the master deed requires.

faqs.q: Can I see the estimate before I make an offer?
faqs.a: Yes. The Pre-Offer Rehab Review is free and is meant for exactly that moment. We estimate repairs from the information available, flag likely hidden conditions common to that type of Boston house, and help you test whether your after-repair value and purchase price leave enough margin. If you buy, the review becomes the starting point for a detailed scope and draw schedule.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Boston, MA | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR renovations in Boston built for the refinance appraisal: triple-decker and two-family rehabs in Dorchester and Roxbury with durable rental-grade finishes.
brrrr.intro:
The BRRRR strategy in Boston almost always runs through a two- or three-family building. The single-family math rarely supports a cash-out refinance at local prices, but a triple-decker in Dorchester or a double-decker in Roxbury can, provided the renovation produces both a strong appraisal and rents that hold up under a lender's income review.

Genstone Construction scopes BRRRR projects with the refinance in mind. That means fixing the items an appraiser and a lender's inspector will look at first, choosing finishes that survive years of tenant turnover, and documenting everything so the refinance file is complete. Genstone Financial, part of the same family of companies, offers DSCR rental loans for investors who want to line up the long-term financing alongside the rehab.

sections.h2: Renovating a triple-decker for the appraisal
sections.body:
Appraisers valuing a renovated Boston triple-decker look at comparable sales of similar buildings and, for income properties, at the rent roll. Both approaches reward the same things: every unit fully renovated rather than one showpiece floor, systems that are clearly updated, and an exterior that does not suggest deferred maintenance.

In practice that often means separate heating systems or a modern central plant, updated electrical service with separate meters, new kitchens and baths in all three units, rebuilt porches and a sound roof. Appraisers will note a fieldstone foundation with active water problems or an obviously original boiler, and those notes can cap the value even when the interiors look good.

We build the scope around what will appear in the appraisal report and the lender's condition review. Where the budget cannot cover everything at once, we help you decide which items move the value and which can wait for a later capital plan, with the estimate showing the cost of each so you can weigh it against the refinance proceeds.

A unit that looks good on refinance day but needs repainting and new flooring after the first tenant is not a BRRRR win. In Dorchester and Roxbury rentals, where units turn regularly and many tenants have children, we favor luxury vinyl plank over carpet, solid-surface or quartz tops, semi-gloss on trim and doors, and fixtures with parts available at any supply house.

Lead compliance is part of durability here. A unit that is properly deleaded under the Massachusetts Lead Law can be rented to any family, which keeps your tenant pool wide and protects the rent roll your lender is underwriting. Replacing old sash windows, which are often the largest lead source, also cuts drafts and heating complaints.

In-unit laundry, separate heat controls and adequate electrical capacity for modern appliances reduce tenant calls and help justify rent at the level your numbers need. Each of these choices is listed in the estimate so you can see how it changes the budget.

Lenders refinancing a Boston rehab often ask for the permits, final inspections and proof that the work was paid in full. A missing ISD sign-off on a boiler or an electrical service upgrade can hold up a closing, and an unpaid subcontractor can create a lien problem at exactly the wrong moment.

Genstone tracks permits and inspections through to final, collects lien waivers as each draw is paid and keeps a photo record of the work from demolition through completion. When it is time to refinance, you have a single package to hand to the lender and appraiser, including the scope, the before-and-after documentation and the inspection history.

If the building was occupied during the rehab, we also document which units were finished when, so the rent roll and the construction record line up. That consistency matters to underwriters looking at a seasoned income property rather than a vacant shell.

faqs.q: Is BRRRR realistic in Boston?
faqs.a: It can be, mostly with two- and three-family buildings bought below market because of condition. The plan works when the renovation adds enough value and rent to support a refinance that returns a meaningful part of your capital. Boston's high prices leave less room for error, so we recommend getting a pre-offer repair estimate and talking with your lender about appraisal and income assumptions before you commit to the purchase.

faqs.q: Should every unit be renovated at once?
faqs.a: For the strongest appraisal, usually yes, because appraisers and lenders view the building as a whole. Some investors renovate the vacant unit first and the others as leases end, accepting a later refinance in exchange for keeping income flowing. We can price both approaches so you can compare the carrying cost against the timing of the refinance and the rent you would lose with all units offline.

faqs.q: Can Genstone help with the refinance itself?
faqs.a: Genstone Construction handles the renovation. Genstone Financial, a sister company, offers DSCR rental loans that are commonly used to refinance out of a rehab loan once the property is stabilized. Using both is optional. Many investors bring their own lender, and we provide the same documentation package either way so the appraisal and underwriting go smoothly. Rate and terms depend on the property and borrower, so compare offers.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Boston, MA | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family and small rental renovations in Boston: tenant-ready turns, deleading, durable finishes and Rental Registry inspection readiness for owners.
rental-renovation.intro:
Rental owners in Boston manage some of the oldest housing in the country under some of the most detailed tenant-protection rules. A good renovation here does two jobs at once: it makes the home durable enough to handle turnover without constant repair calls, and it brings the unit up to the standards inspectors, tenants and the Massachusetts Lead Law expect.

Genstone Construction renovates single-family rentals, condos held as rentals and small portfolio homes across Boston, from West Roxbury Capes to Hyde Park Victorians. Individual owners, property managers and investment funds use us to standardize finishes, cut turn costs and keep documentation consistent across properties. Each project gets a written scope, a designated field manager and draws tied to completed work, with no upfront payment.

sections.h2: A finish standard built for Boston turnover
sections.body:
Portfolio owners get the best results when every rental shares a common specification: the same flooring, paint colors, cabinet line, fixtures and appliance models wherever practical. In Boston that standard needs to account for older buildings with uneven floors, plaster walls and odd-sized windows, so we choose materials that install well over imperfect substrates.

A typical spec for a Boston rental might include luxury vinyl plank that tolerates out-of-level floors, durable flat or eggshell walls with semi-gloss trim, solid-surface counters, and mid-grade fixtures from widely stocked lines. Bathrooms get exhaust fans vented outside, because old houses with tight new windows quickly develop moisture and mold problems without them.

Standardization pays off at every turn afterward. Touch-up paint, replacement planks and fixture parts are on hand, maintenance techs know the products, and estimates for future turns become predictable. We document the spec so it can be applied consistently across your Boston homes and any others in the region.

sections.h2: Inspection readiness and Boston rental rules
sections.body:
Boston requires most non-owner-occupied rental units to be registered with the city, and ISD conducts periodic rental inspections under that program. Inspectors look for working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, safe egress, adequate heat, functioning plumbing and electrical, and the absence of obvious hazards like peeling paint or missing handrails.

We build those items into every rental renovation. That includes interconnected smoke and CO alarms where required, secure stair and porch railings, GFCI protection in kitchens and baths, and heating systems that can reliably meet the state sanitary code's temperature requirements during the heating season.

For homes built before 1978, we also plan for lead. If a family with young children could rent the unit, deleading under state rules avoids the risk of having to stop and do it later under a deadline. Building these items into a planned renovation is far less disruptive than reacting to an inspection report or a tenant complaint.

sections.h2: Turning units quickly between Boston leases
sections.body:
Many Boston leases still turn over around September 1, especially near the universities in Brighton, Allston, Jamaica Plain and the Fenway, which compresses an entire year's worth of turns into a few hectic weeks. Owners who wait until August to line up contractors often end up with units sitting empty into the fall.

We help portfolio owners plan turn work ahead of those dates, walking units as soon as notice is given and pricing the scope while the tenant is still in place where access allows. Painters, flooring crews and cleaners are scheduled in sequence, and any larger repairs found at move-out are estimated quickly so you can approve them without delaying the next tenant.

Genstone Field Services, a sister company, handles occupied maintenance, inspections and turn and make-ready work, which gives owners one coordinated team for both capital renovations and recurring turns. Students and young professionals in Allston and Brighton are hard on units, so the turn scope there usually leans toward repairable, replaceable surfaces.

faqs.q: Do you work with property managers?
faqs.a: Yes. Property managers often send us units at move-out or when an owner approves a larger renovation. We provide a written scope and estimate the manager can share with the owner, keep the manager updated through the job and deliver photos and documentation at completion. Communication can run through the manager, the owner or both, depending on how your agreement is set up.

faqs.q: What is not covered by the workmanship warranty?
faqs.a: Genstone provides a one-year workmanship warranty on completed work. It covers defects in how the work was performed. It does not cover damage caused by tenants or normal wear and tear, which in rentals can be significant. Choosing durable, rental-grade finishes is the best way to keep those costs down, and we can recommend a specification for your Boston properties with that in mind.

faqs.q: Can you renovate rentals in nearby cities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Our network covers Greater Boston, including Cambridge, Somerville, Quincy, Malden and other nearby communities, and the same finish standard and documentation process applies across them. Owners with properties throughout Massachusetts and other states use a single scope format and reporting process for the entire portfolio, which makes budgeting and asset management much easier. Brookline, Milton and Chelsea are covered as well.

multifamily-renovation.title: Triple-Decker & 2-4 Unit Renovation in Boston | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Boston two-family and triple-decker renovations: phased work around tenants, shared boilers, porches, fire separation and ISD permits for 2-4 unit investors.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Two- to Four-Unit Renovations in Boston
multifamily-renovation.intro:
Small multifamily is the heart of Boston's investor market. The triple-decker and the two-family double-decker make up a large share of the housing in Dorchester, Roxbury, Jamaica Plain, East Boston and South Boston, and their stacked layout creates renovation questions a single-family rehab never faces: one roof over three households, a shared basement full of mechanicals, porches that serve as fire escapes, and tenants who still need heat while you work.

Genstone Construction renovates two- to four-unit buildings across Boston for owner-occupant investors, small landlords and funds. We scope each unit and the common systems separately so you can see what the building needs as a whole and what each apartment needs on its own, then phase the work to match your leases and financing.

sections.h2: Shared systems in stacked Boston buildings
sections.body:
Most triple-deckers were built with a single coal boiler and later converted to oil or gas, often with one heating system serving all three floors. That arrangement makes it hard to bill tenants for heat and leaves the whole building cold if the boiler fails. Many renovations separate the heat into individual systems per unit, using gas boilers, furnaces or ductless heat pumps, and separate the electrical service into individual meters.

The roof, foundation, front and rear porches, and the exterior envelope are shared as well. These are usually the most expensive items in a multifamily scope, and they affect every unit's value. A leaking roof will damage the third floor no matter how nice its new kitchen is.

We price building-wide systems and unit interiors as separate line items, which lets you plan a phased approach if needed and gives lenders a clear picture of the capital going into the asset.

sections.h2: Renovating around tenants in Dorchester and Roxbury
sections.body:
Investors frequently buy Boston multifamilies with one or two units occupied. Renovating the vacant unit first, then moving through the building as leases turn, keeps income coming in but requires careful planning. Work in the basement, on the service entrance or on a shared boiler can interrupt heat, water or power for everyone.

Your field manager schedules disruptive work in short, announced windows, coordinates access with tenants and keeps common hallways and porches safe and passable. Dust control and lead-safe work practices are especially important when tenants, possibly including children, live in the building during the job.

Massachusetts gives tenants strong protections, and the state sanitary code sets minimum standards for heat, hot water and habitability during occupancy. We plan the sequence so the building stays compliant throughout. That way the renovation does not create tenant complaints, code calls or rent issues that undercut the value you are trying to add.

The stacked porches on a Boston triple-decker are more than outdoor space. The rear porch and stair often serve as the second means of egress for the upper units, and inspectors treat them that way. Rotted posts, rusted fasteners and undersized footings are common after decades of winter weather, and rebuilding porches is one of the most frequent permit items in multifamily rehabs here.

Inside, balloon-framed walls and open stairwells can let fire travel between floors. When walls are opened, we add fire blocking at floor lines and coordinate with ISD on fire-separation requirements between units, especially where a building is being converted to condos or units are being reconfigured.

Interconnected smoke and carbon monoxide alarms across all units are standard, and the Boston Fire Department's certificate is needed before any sale. Planning these life-safety items early prevents surprises at rough and final inspections and keeps the project moving. Basement-to-attic stair enclosures deserve a look too.

faqs.q: Can you convert a Boston triple-decker to condos?
faqs.a: We handle the construction side of condo conversions, including utility separation, fire separation between units, egress improvements and unit renovations. Zoning relief, condo documents and any tenant notification requirements are handled by your attorney and design team. We coordinate with them so the construction scope matches the plans approved by the city and the needs of future unit buyers and their lenders.

faqs.q: Is it worth separating the heat in a two-family?
faqs.a: Often it is. Separate heating lets tenants pay their own heating costs, reduces disputes over temperature and spreads the risk of a single boiler failure. The cost depends on the existing system and whether gas service, ductwork or heat pumps are practical in your building. We can price separate-system options alongside a central boiler replacement so you can compare them against your rents and operating plans.

faqs.q: Do you work on four-unit buildings?
faqs.a: Yes. Two-, three- and four-unit buildings are all within our scope, including the brick and wood-frame four-families found in parts of Dorchester, Brighton and East Boston. Larger buildings follow the same approach of separating building-wide systems from unit interiors, with phasing planned around occupancy and financing. Brick four-families in Brighton, for example, often need masonry repointing, flat roof work and stairwell upgrades along with unit interiors, and we scope those as building-wide items so your lender sees the full plan.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Boston, MA | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor in Boston: bids, consultant coordination and draws for Standard and Limited 203(k) loans on Boston two-families and older homes.
fha-203k.intro:
For many Boston buyers, an FHA 203(k) loan is the realistic way into a house that needs real work, especially an owner-occupied two- or three-family where the rent from the other units helps carry the mortgage. The program rolls renovation costs into the purchase loan, but it also adds paperwork, inspections and lender rules that many contractors avoid.

Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor. We work with buyers, real estate agents, loan officers and 203(k) consultants to produce bids that meet lender requirements, schedule the work around the draw process and document each phase. Boston's older housing, with its lead paint, old wiring and aging heating systems, is exactly where a well-scoped 203(k) loan makes the most sense.

sections.h2: Standard or Limited 203(k) for a Boston house
sections.body:
The Limited 203(k) covers non-structural repairs up to $75,000, making it a good fit for homes that need updates rather than major changes: a new boiler, kitchen and bath updates, window replacement, flooring, paint and lead hazard work. Many Roslindale, Hyde Park and West Roxbury single-families fall into this category.

The Standard 203(k) is designed for larger or structural projects, with a minimum repair amount of $5,000, and it requires a HUD-approved 203(k) consultant. It fits Boston projects such as triple-deckers needing new porches, foundation repair, layout changes or full system replacement. The consultant prepares the work write-up, reviews contractor bids and inspects the work before draws are released.

We help buyers and agents determine which loan type the property is likely to need by walking through the scope early. Starting with the right program avoids having to restructure the loan after an offer is accepted. A Hyde Park Victorian with a failing porch foundation, for example, is usually a Standard loan even if the interiors only need cosmetic work.

sections.h2: Which Boston homes fit the program
sections.body:
Owner-occupied two- and three-families are among the strongest 203(k) candidates in Boston. FHA allows financing of one- to four-unit properties when the buyer lives in one of the units, so a buyer can purchase a Dorchester or Roxbury triple-decker, renovate all units and use the rental income to help with the payment.

These buildings often need exactly what the program is designed to fund: updated heating and electrical systems, porch reconstruction, roof replacement and work to meet FHA's minimum property requirements. Lead paint is a significant consideration, since FHA requires deteriorated paint in pre-1978 homes to be addressed, and the Massachusetts Lead Law applies if children under six will live there.

Single-family Capes and Colonials in West Roxbury, Hyde Park and Roslindale are also good candidates, especially homes with original kitchens, old windows and outdated systems that discourage conventional buyers. Gas service availability, an aging oil tank or a slate roof can tip a Boston property from Limited to Standard, so we flag those items early.

sections.h2: Bids, consultants and draws in Boston
sections.body:
A 203(k) bid has to be detailed enough for the lender and consultant to match it line by line against the work write-up. We provide itemized pricing, materials, quantities and a draw schedule, which helps loans close on time.

During construction, draws are released after the consultant or lender's inspector verifies completed work. On Limited loans, repair amounts above $15,000 typically trigger inspection requirements before funds are released. We schedule work and documentation to match these inspection points so payments are not delayed.

ISD permits and inspections run alongside the 203(k) process. We pull permits, coordinate inspections and collect lien waivers with each draw. For buyers, that means a clear schedule and a single point of contact. For agents and loan officers, it means fewer surprises between contract and closing and a renovation that finishes in line with the loan. When change orders come up, such as rotted sills found behind clapboard, we document them for the consultant and lender before proceeding.

faqs.q: Can I use a 203(k) loan on a Boston triple-decker?
faqs.a: Yes, provided you will live in one of the units as your primary residence. FHA allows financing on one- to four-unit properties for owner-occupants, and a 203(k) loan can include renovation of all units. Your lender will look at the property's value after renovation and other factors when sizing the loan. We can scope the full building early so you and your loan officer know what the renovation budget needs to cover.

faqs.q: Do you work with 203(k) consultants?
faqs.a: Yes. On Standard 203(k) loans, a HUD-approved consultant is required, and we coordinate with them throughout. That includes responding to the work write-up, adjusting bids where needed and scheduling work around their draw inspections. Agents and lenders often find that having a contractor experienced with the process makes the consultant's job easier and keeps closings on track. We also answer consultant questions quickly.

faqs.q: Who are your 203(k) clients in Boston?
faqs.a: Our 203(k) work typically comes from homebuyers, buyer's agents and loan officers who need a contractor comfortable with the program's documentation and draw process. Agents often bring us in before the offer so the buyer understands the likely renovation cost. Loan officers refer us when they need bids that meet lender standards and a contractor who can deliver on schedule.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Boston, MA | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO renovation for banks, servicers and GSEs in Boston: freeze and mold remediation, code violations, vacant property registration and documented repairs.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovations in Boston
reo-renovation.intro:
Bank-owned properties in Boston are usually old buildings that sat through at least one winter without regular care. By the time a servicer or lender takes control, the problems tend to follow a pattern: burst pipes from a failed winterization, mold in a wet basement, porches and stairs that have deteriorated, and open ISD violations that need resolving before the property can be sold or rented.

Genstone Construction works with banks, mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, for which we are a preferred contractor. Our process is built around what asset managers need: fast, documented property assessments, clear repair estimates with options, compliant work through licensed local contractors and detailed photo and invoice documentation for every step.

sections.h2: Common conditions in vacant Boston properties
sections.body:
Freeze damage is the most common major problem in Boston REOs. Older homes with plumbing in exterior walls, unheated porches and basements with poor insulation are vulnerable when heat is lost during the winter. A failed winterization can lead to split pipes, cracked boilers and water damage across multiple floors in a triple-decker.

Mold often follows. Fieldstone basements that already take on water during snowmelt, combined with standing water from burst pipes, can quickly grow mold on framing, drywall and stored belongings. Remediation, drying and correcting the water source are typically the first steps in a scope.

Vacant buildings also attract break-ins, copper theft and illegal occupancy, especially in multifamily properties. Securing the property, replacing stolen piping and wiring and restoring damaged doors and windows may be needed before other repairs can begin. Each finding is photographed and documented so asset managers can make decisions without traveling to the site.

sections.h2: Vacant property registration and code compliance
sections.body:
Boston requires owners of vacant and foreclosing residential properties to register them with the city and maintain them to minimum standards. Servicers and lenders taking control of a Boston property should expect inspections and enforcement if the property becomes a nuisance, and an open violation can complicate a sale.

We review ISD records for open violations and address them as part of the scope, including issues like unsafe porches, missing smoke detectors, exterior debris and unsecured openings. Where permits are needed for repairs, we handle filing, inspections and closeout so the property's record is clean when it goes to market.

Genstone Field Services, a sister company, provides property preservation, inspections and code compliance services, which can bridge the gap between initial securing of a property and its full renovation. Using a coordinated team reduces handoffs and keeps documentation consistent across the property's history. Boston's older housing makes many of these violations predictable, and catching them early saves time.

sections.h2: Repair strategy for Boston REO dispositions
sections.body:
The right repair scope for a bank-owned property depends on how it will be sold. Some Boston REOs are best sold to investors in as-is condition after only safety and code repairs, while others will bring more money as financeable homes after systems and finishes are updated.

We provide estimates at different levels, typically a minimum scope focused on safety, securing and code, along with a full renovation option designed to meet FHA or conventional lending standards. That allows asset managers to compare the cost of each approach with the expected sale price and holding time.

For multifamily REOs, we also consider occupancy. Buildings with tenants in place may need repairs to meet the state sanitary code before anything else. Every scope includes photos, line-item pricing, lien waivers and a clear schedule, which supports the internal approval processes and audit requirements that servicers and GSEs depend on. In neighborhoods like Mattapan and Hyde Park, a financeable renovation can widen the buyer pool considerably.

faqs.q: Do you work directly with asset managers?
faqs.a: Yes. Most of our REO work comes from asset managers at banks, servicers, funds and GSEs. We provide estimates in a format that supports their approval process, offer repair options when appropriate, and keep them informed through photos and progress updates. Our team can also work with field service vendors and listing brokers already assigned to a property. Bid formats can follow your platform's requirements.

faqs.q: Can you handle properties with open code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Resolving ISD violations is a common part of our REO work in Boston. We review the violation record, include corrective work in the scope, pull required permits and schedule inspections to close out the issues. Documentation is provided at each stage, which helps servicers demonstrate compliance and avoid additional penalties or delays in disposing of the property. Boston violations are often porch-related.

faqs.q: What happens when a REO has freeze damage?
faqs.a: We begin by assessing the damage, stopping any active leaks, drying the property and checking for mold. Then we scope plumbing, heating and finish repairs, and we provide photos and estimates to the asset manager for approval. In multifamily buildings, we check each unit separately, since freeze damage often affects floors differently. Winterization or temporary heat can be included to prevent further damage.
